# @zakkster/lite-clock

Zero-GC simulation/timeline engine for @zakkster/lite-signal. SOA TypedArray
lane pool. Deterministic `advance(dt)` -- the only mutation entry point.
Single force-propagate frame signal carrying simTime; lane reads pull values
directly from TypedArrays so 10K lanes cost one signal write per tick.

Single-file ESM, ~480 LOC, MIT, zero runtime deps, peer dep `lite-signal ^1.2.0`.

## Install

    npm install @zakkster/lite-clock @zakkster/lite-signal

## Imports

    import { createClock, LiteClockCapacityError } from "@zakkster/lite-clock";

## Exports

### `createClock(config?)`

Factory. Returns a frozen `Clock` instance.

Config (all optional):
- `capacity: number` -- initial pool size. Default 1024, max 65534. Must be a
  positive integer.
- `growable: boolean` -- when true, the pool doubles on exhaustion (up to
  65534). Default false (throws).

Validation throws `TypeError` (shape) / `RangeError` (value) up front.

### `clock.advance(dt: number): void`

The ONLY mutation entry point. Validates `Number.isFinite(dt) && dt >= 0`
(throws `RangeError` otherwise). `dt=0` still increments `ticks` and
force-propagates the frame signal so subscribers observe the call.

Tick phases:
1. Validate dt
2. simTime += dt; tickCount++
3. In-place active-list compaction: iterate activeList, write positions back
   for survivors, queue completedIds for end-of-tick drain
4. `frameSig.set(simTime)` -- force-propagate (equals: () => false)
5. Drain onComplete queue (callbacks fire AFTER signal propagation)

Re-entrant: onComplete callbacks may call any clock method, including
advance(), lane(), etc. The active loop has finished by callback time.

### `clock.advanceTo(t: number): void`

Advance simTime to absolute `t`. Throws if `t < simTime`. `t === simTime` is
a no-op tick (dt=0 behavior).

### `clock.lane(opts): Lane`

Allocate a new lane from the pool.

Opts:
- `duration: number` -- > 0, in sim-time units (typically ms)
- `onComplete?: () => void` -- fires once in the end-of-tick queue

Throws `LiteClockCapacityError` if the pool is exhausted and `growable: false`.

### `Lane` (handle)

Methods:
- `start()` -- begin advancing (or resume from a pause). Idempotent.
- `pause()` -- stop advancing; snapshots `positions[id] = elapsed`. Idempotent.
- `reverse()` -- toggle direction-of-reporting for position()/t(). Idempotent.
- `dispose()` -- free the slot back to the pool. Idempotent. Subsequent method
  calls on the handle are silent no-ops.

Reads (tracked -- register dependency on the clock's frame signal):
- `position(): number` -- sim-time units, [0..duration]
- `t(): number` -- normalized [0..1]
- `done(): boolean`

Reads (untracked):
- `positionPeek(): number`
- `tPeek(): number`
- `donePeek(): boolean`

Reverse mode: the engine advances `elapsed` forward always. `reverse()` flips
what `position()`/`t()`/peek variants return. Completion fires on forward
`elapsed >= duration` regardless of reverse flag -- a reversed lane "rewinds
to start" and completes at `t === 0`.

### `clock.frame: FrameAccessor`

`ReadSignal`-shaped accessor for simTime:
- `clock.frame(): number` -- tracked
- `clock.frame.peek(): number`
- `clock.frame.subscribe(fn): Dispose`

Force-propagates on every advance (even dt=0).

### `clock.attachRAF(): void`

Drive from `requestAnimationFrame`. Computes dt from the rAF timestamp.
Throws if rAF is not available (e.g. plain Node).

### `clock.attachInterval(ms: number): void`

Drive from `setInterval`. Computes dt from `performance.now()` between fires.
Node-side handles are `.unref()`'d so they don't block process exit.

### `clock.detach(): void`

Cancel any attached tick source. Idempotent.

Each attach call replaces any prior attach.

### `clock.dispose(): void`

Returns the frame signal's node to the lite-signal pool, detaches any
attached tick source, and resets the lane pool. Idempotent.

**Required** for bounded-lifetime clocks (per route, per level, per
component mount) -- without it every `createClock()`/`dispose()` cycle leaks
one slot from the lite-signal default registry and the 1024th cycle hits
`CapacityError`.

### `clock.simTime: number` (read-only)
### `clock.ticks: number` (read-only)
### `clock.capacity: number` (read-only)
### `clock.activeCount: number` (read-only)

Plain getters. Not signals -- if you need reactivity, track `clock.frame()`.

### `LiteClockCapacityError`

Extends `Error`. Thrown by `clock.lane()` on pool exhaustion. Carries:
- `name: "LiteClockCapacityError"`
- `capacity: number` -- the pool size that was exhausted

Message names both escape hatches (`{ capacity: N }` and `{ growable: true }`).

## Key invariants

- `advance(dt)` is the only mutation entry point. dt validation is up-front;
  the hot loop has no per-iter validation.
- One force-propagate frame signal per clock. Lane reads pull from TypedArrays
  routed through clock getters (so growth-relocated arrays are transparent
  to live LaneHandle instances).
- In-place active-list compaction. Completed lanes drop out without a second
  pass.
- Frame signal propagates BEFORE onComplete callbacks fire. Effects tracking
  `lane.done()` see `true` BEFORE the callback runs.
- Re-entrant safe: onComplete callbacks may call any clock method.
- Pool is LIFO (free list is a stack). Most-recently-disposed slot is reused
  first.
- Reverse only affects reporting. Engine always advances elapsed forward.
- Pool exhaustion throws by default; `growable: true` doubles up to 65534.
- `clock.dispose()` is required for bounded-lifetime clocks (releases the
  frame signal node back to the lite-signal pool).

## Common patterns

### DOM animation driven by a lane

    import { effect } from "@zakkster/lite-signal";
    import { createClock } from "@zakkster/lite-clock";

    const clock = createClock();
    clock.attachRAF();

    const lane = clock.lane({ duration: 300 });
    effect(() => { el.style.opacity = lane.t(); });
    lane.start();

### Chained transitions via onComplete

    const fade = clock.lane({
        duration: 200,
        onComplete: () => {
            const next = clock.lane({ duration: 300, onComplete: finish });
            next.start();
        }
    });
    fade.start();

### Deterministic test playback

    const clock = createClock();
    const lane = clock.lane({ duration: 100 });
    lane.start();
    [16.67, 33.33, 16.67, 8.33].forEach((dt) => clock.advance(dt));
    // simTime, position, done are 100% reproducible.

### Multi-clock for isolated subsystems

    const ui  = createClock(); ui.attachRAF();          // 60fps animations
    const sim = createClock(); sim.attachInterval(8);   // 125Hz physics

### Composition with lite-statechart

    const clock = createClock(); clock.attachRAF();
    let pulse;
    const machine = createStatechart({
        initial: "idle",
        states: {
            idle:    { entry: () => pulse?.dispose(), on: { START: "active" } },
            active:  {
                entry: () => {
                    pulse = clock.lane({
                        duration: 1000,
                        onComplete: () => machine.send("DONE")
                    });
                    pulse.start();
                },
                on: { STOP: "idle", DONE: "idle" }
            }
        }
    });

## What this is NOT

- Not a tween library (no easing curves -- compose with `lite-ease`)
- Not a state machine (compose with `lite-statechart`)
- Not async (no promises, no microtasks)
- Not a renderer (only computes lane positions)
- Not a scheduler with priorities (all lanes advance at the clock's rate)

## Deterministic testing

`advance(dt)` is the sole mutation entry point. Inject any dt sequence twice
in two fresh clocks and you get identical state. `attachRAF` and
`attachInterval` are convenience wrappers that compute dt from real time and
call `advance()`; tests should use `advance()` directly.

## Files

- `Clock.js` -- implementation (~480 lines, ESM)
- `Clock.d.ts` -- TypeScript declarations
- `test/01..11` -- behavior, GC, dispose-leak regression suites
- `bench/bench.mjs` -- six-scenario throughput + retention measurement
- `README.md` -- full architecture + integration recipes
- `CHANGELOG.md` -- versioned change log
- `ROADMAP.md` -- deferred features and rationale
